title: Sacchi's 25 Metres
subtitle: How Milan pressed: one distance, one trigger, one trap

acts.title: Twenty-five metres
acts.caption: The block is not a shape. It is a distance.
acts.notes: The back four is on the halfway line and the front two are 25 metres ahead of them. Sacchi allowed no more than that, ever. Everything else in this system is a consequence of the one number: the pressing is possible because the distances are short, and the line can step because there is nobody stranded behind it.

texts.text:
The distance
is the system.

acts.title: What everybody else did
acts.caption: Everybody else defended 45 metres. Sacchi refused to defend more than 25.
acts.notes: Italian football in 1987 defended a much bigger piece of grass than this. A deep back line, a libero behind it to clean up, and forty-five metres of open pitch between the last defender and the centre-forward. Sacchi did not invent pressing. He halved the distance it had to be done over, which is what made it survivable.

texts.text:
Everybody else defended
forty-five metres.

acts.title: Four reference points
acts.caption: The ball. The space. The opponent. His own team-mate.
acts.notes: Sacchi's players moved in relation to four things at once, and decided which of the four owned the movement. Nobody in this side is marking a man. The left midfielder is holding a distance to the ball, a distance to the team-mate inside him, a distance to the winger outside him, and a piece of grass.

texts.text:
the ball
the space
the opponent
his team-mate

acts.title: One body
acts.caption: The ball moves 16 metres. All eleven move it with it.
acts.notes: The ball is played square across their two centre-backs and the entire block slides with it, the same distance, in the same direction, at the same moment. The shape does not change. This is the drill Milan did without a ball, on a rope, for hours, and it is the reason nobody in the block ever has to run to recover.

texts.text:
One body.
Not eleven players.

acts.title: The middle is already shut
acts.caption: Nobody dives in. The inside passes are closed by where men stand.
acts.notes: "Pressing is not about running and it is not about working hard. It is about controlling space. Force the opposition to pass where you want them to." The nine shows the centre-back the touchline with the angle of his approach; the ten covers the pivot behind him. Neither of them is trying to win the ball here.

texts.text:
Nobody dives in.
The lanes are shut.

acts.title: What it costs if one man goes
acts.caption: If one man goes early, the pass goes past him and the block has a hole in it.
acts.notes: This is the failure the whole system is built to avoid, and it is worth showing because it is the only way to explain why the pressing looks so patient. The nine commits, gets there half a second early, and the centre-back plays into the space he left. Nobody behind him has moved, so the hole is real. Sacchi fined it.

texts.text:
One man dives in.
The system is gone.

acts.title: The trigger is the pass to the full-back
acts.caption: One pass. Eleven minds. The whole side leans before it arrives.
acts.notes: The press was not started by a whistle or by a mistake. It was started by a specific pass, out to the full-back, the weakest passer on the pitch, in the narrowest part of it. The side moves on the pass, not on the reception.

texts.text:
They think
they chose it.

acts.title: The half second before
acts.caption: Six men are already moving. The ball has not landed.
acts.notes: This is the frame that separates the system from a hard-working team. The ball is still travelling and the trap is already three-quarters built. Nobody is reacting to the full-back receiving it, because by then it is too late to arrive together.

texts.text:
The ball has not
landed yet.

acts.title: Three men arrive at once
acts.caption: Not one presser. Three, and the touchline.
acts.notes: The left midfielder takes the ball, the left-back steps out onto the winger behind him, the six slides across to seal the inside, and the nine drops on the pass back to the centre-back. Four outfield players inside a twenty-metre square, and the far side of the pitch deliberately empty.

texts.text:
The touchline is
the fourth defender.

acts.title: Four ways out, all of them shut
acts.caption: Back, inside, down the line, or the winger. There is a man on all four.
acts.notes: A press is only a press when it takes the options away rather than the time. The full-back has four passes available and every one of them arrives at a Milan player, so he has the ball, the touchline, and nothing to do with either.

texts.text:
Four ways out.
All four are shut.

acts.title: We give them the far side on purpose
acts.caption: The switch is the only ball out. It is 53 metres, first time, with a man on him.
acts.notes: The far winger tucks in rather than holding his touchline, so the block is eleven men on one half of the grass. The far flank is genuinely open, and that is the trade: the only ball that punishes it is a long switch, first time, played by a full-back with three men on him.

texts.text:
Eleven men on
half the grass.

acts.title: He plays it, and it still does not work
acts.caption: The ball travels 54 metres. The block travels 20, and gets there first.
acts.notes: The honest version of the trade. He does find the switch and it does arrive. But a ball that spends that long in the air is a ball the block has time to travel with, and the man who receives it on the far touchline has a Milan player on him before he can take a second touch. The far side was never free. It was only far.

texts.text:
It arrives.
So do we.

acts.title: The one ball he has left
acts.caption: He cannot go back, inside or down the line. So he loads the only ball left.
acts.notes: The back four has squared up at 62 metres and the centre-forward has dropped onto the last man to stay legal. He is onside. Everything up to this point has been about removing the short passes, and it has worked: the only ball left is the one over the top, which is the ball this defence wants him to choose.

texts.text:
ONSIDE
BY 2

He has one ball left.
Over the top.

acts.title: Attacking their attack
acts.caption: The four go together. 8 metres, on one call, before the ball is struck.
acts.notes: Baresi calls it and the four go together, before the ball is struck rather than after it, because the law judges where the attacker stands at the moment of the pass. The centre-forward turns and runs back and does not get there. Offside stopped being a way of surviving a ball over the top and became a way of taking possession back.

texts.text:
OFFSIDE
BY 2

Offside is not a defence.
It is an attack.

acts.title: Two metres
acts.caption: At the moment the pass leaves, he is 2 metres the wrong side of it.
acts.notes: The pass leaves and the ball runs through into grass that belongs to nobody. He is not thirteen metres out and stranded, he is two metres out and beaten, which is what the trap is for: it is decided by a call and a stride, not by a mistake.

texts.text:
OFFSIDE
BY 2

acts.title: Seventy metres, and one goalkeeper
acts.caption: 70 metres behind the line, and one goalkeeper in it. That is the price.
acts.notes: The price, on its own frame, because a system that only shows what it wins is a sales pitch. There is more grass behind this back four than most sides defend in total, and one man in it. It is not defended by a sweeper. It is defended by a law and by four players agreeing, every single time, on when to move.

texts.text:
OFFSIDE
BY 2

Nobody is defending it.
The law is.

acts.title: Or he gives it away
acts.caption: The ball is won 32 metres from his goal. That is what the 25 metres bought.
acts.notes: The trap has two endings and both of them hand us the ball. This is the one that hurts: the turnover happens in the corner the full-back was pressed into, and the channel he came from has nobody in it. Two strikers, one pass, and the defence is facing its own goal.

texts.text:
Two strikers.
One pass.

acts.title: That is what the distance bought
acts.caption: Won 32 metres out. One pass later it is a shot from 17.
acts.notes: The argument for the whole system, in one number. A side that wins the ball on its own edge of the box has to play through a set defence to hurt anybody. A side that wins it here is already in a shooting position, against a back four running the wrong way. Sacchi never called this a defensive system, and it is not one.

texts.text:
Win it there and it is
already a chance.
